{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
{{short description|British mathematician, clergyman, and schoolmaster}}
'''Benjamin Pulleyne''', ''sometimes spelt'' '''Pullan''' (30 September 1785 – 20 October 1861), was a mathematician, [[Church of England]] clergyman, fellow of [[Clare College, Cambridge]], and [[schoolmaster]]. For almost fifty years he was the Master of [[Gresham's School]], then usually known as Holt Grammar School.

<div style="float:right;clear:right">[[File:20130808 Castle End from Kings Bridge.jpg|thumb|200px|Clare College, Cambridge]]</div>
Born at [[Scarborough, North Yorkshire]], the son of Benjamin Pullan, a merchant, and his wife Elizabeth,<ref>"Benjamin Pullan" in ''England & Wales, Christening Index, 1530–1980'', ancestry.com, accessed 3 December 2020: "Benjamin Pullan / Gender: Male / Christening Age: 0 / Birth Date: 30 Sep 1785 / Christening Date: 30 Oct 1785 / Christening Place: Scarborough, Yorkshire, England / Father: Benjamin Pullan / Mother:	Elizabeth Pullan" {{subscription required}}</ref><ref name=Wedding1853>Marriages Solemnized at the Parish Church of Buckenham in the County of Norfolk, 1853,  [https://www.ancestry.co.uk/imageviewer/collections/61043/images/61043_b938727-00005 No. 9, July 12, 1853], ancestry.co.uk, accessed 3 December 2020 {{subscription required}}</ref> the young Pulleyne (the spelling of the name he used for himself) was educated at [[Queen Elizabeth Grammar School, Wakefield|Wakefield Grammar School]] and was admitted to Clare College, Cambridge, on 2 February 1804.<ref name=JV>"PULLAN (or PULLEYNE), Benjamin", in [[John Venn]], ''[[Alumni Cantabrigienses]]'' Part II. 1752–1900, 
Vol. V Pace – Spyers (1953), [https://archive.org/details/p2alumnicantabri05univuoft/p2alumnicantabri05univuoft/page/215/mode/1up p. 215]</ref>
He was elected a Cave Scholar on 19 January 1805 and was [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|Senior Optime]] in 1808.<ref name=MP>Matthew Peacock, ''The History of Wakefield Grammar School'' (Milnes, 1892), p. 182: this calls him "Master of Holt Grammar School, Norfolk".</ref>

He graduated [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in 1808, promoted by seniority to [[Master of Arts (Oxford, Cambridge, and Dublin)|MA]] in 1811, and was a Fellow of his college from 1808 to 1809. Becoming a [[deacon]] of the Church of England in 1808, he was ordained as a priest in 1810 by [[Henry Bathurst (bishop)|Henry Bathurst]], [[Bishop of Norwich]].<ref name=JV/> This was at a time when most academics at Oxford were obliged to lead celibate lives in college and had to resign their fellowships if they wished to marry.

<div style="float:right;clear:right">[[File:Old School House, Holt, 1838.jpg|thumb|200px|Holt Grammar School in 1838]]</div> Pulleyne was [[List of masters of Gresham's School|Master of Holt Grammar School]] from 1809 to 1857,<ref name=JV/> the salary for which was £200 a year.<ref>''City of London Livery Companies' Commission: Report and Appendix'', Volume 4, ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=vuwUAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA237 p. 237]''</ref> Having held the post for 48 years, he remains the school's longest-serving head since its foundation in 1555.<ref>S. G. G. Benson, Martin Crossley Evans, ''I Will Plant Me a Tree: an Illustrated History of Gresham's School'' (James & James, London, 2002)</ref> He was also Vicar of [[Sheringham]] from 1825 until his death, and of [[Weybourne, Norfolk|Weybourne]] from 1845.<ref name=JV/>

John William Burgon, in ''The Life and Times of Sir Thomas Gresham'' (1839), says {{Blockquote|Holt school... is an ornament and a blessing to the county, and reflects much credit on the trustees and its worthy principal—the Rev. B. Pulleyne.<ref>John William Burgon, ''The Life and Times of Sir Thomas Gresham: Comp. Chiefly from His Correspondence Preserved in Her Majesty's Statepaper Office: Including Notices of Many of His Contemporaries'' (R. Jennings, 1839), [https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_0uoJAAAAIAAJ/page/n42 p. 15]</ref>}}

==Personal life==
At the [[1851 United Kingdom census|census of March 1851]], Pulleyne was living at 38, Market Place, Holt, with his wife Rebecca, who was blind, his son Walter M. Pulleyne, aged 34, an [[apothecary]], his daughter in law, his seven-year-old granddaughter Anne, and two servants.<ref>[[1851 United Kingdom census]], [https://www.ancestry.co.uk/imageviewer/collections/8860/images/NFKHO107_1809_1810-0032 Market Place, Holt], ancestry.co.uk, accessed 2 December 2020</ref> His wife, Rebecca Pulleyne, died at Holt on 13 March 1853.<ref>''[[The Gentleman's Magazine]]'', Volume 193 (1853), [https://books.google.com/books?id=QUJDAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA561 p. 561]: "March 13... At Holt, Norfolk, Rebecca, wife of the Rev. Benjamin Pulleyne."</ref> On 12 July of the same year, at [[Buckenham]], Norfolk, Pulleyne married Mary Dinah Partridge, a farmer's daughter.<ref name=Wedding1853/><ref>"Partridge, Mary Dinah / Blofield / 4b 345"; "Pulleyne, Benjamin / Blofield / 4b 345" in ''General Index to Marriages in England and Wales'' (September quarter, 1853)</ref>

Having retired from his school, Pulleyne then lived at Sheringham, where he died in October 1861. He left a widow, Mary Dinah.<ref>"Pulleyne, the Reverend Benjamin", in ''Wills and Administrations 1861'' (England and Wales Probate Office, 1862)</ref>
